title: Sign out idle sessions
subtitle: A pre-read: the idea first, then the order to read the code in

scenes.narration: Today a session lasts thirty days, even on a shared computer nobody has touched in a week. This change also ends a session after thirty minutes without a request.
scenes.summary: End a session after **30 minutes** without a request, and still after 30 days at most
bullets: Every request now pushes the idle limit back, which is one more Redis call
Saving a session resets its start time, which may stretch the 30-day cap
A stale cookie is now cleared from the browser

scenes.title: A session with a long lunch
scenes.narration: Follow one session through a morning with a lunch break.

steps.say: Signing in starts a thirty minute idle limit.
Each page they open pushes that limit back by another thirty minutes.
Then they go to lunch. Thirty minutes after the last page, the session ends.
Back from lunch, they sign in again, and the browser's old cookie is cleared.

scenes.narration: Read the session store first, since it holds both limits. Then where sign-in and profile edits save a session, the middleware that clears old cookies, and the new tests. The docs are routine.

items.check: `save` resets `createdAt`, so a busy session may outlive the 30-day cap
`updateProfile` calls `save` too, which restarts the 30 days
no cookie skips Redis; a cookie with no session is cleared
covers the idle limit; nothing tests the 30-day cap
`SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES` is 30 and is not read from the environment
